answer.rationale:
The presenting symptoms are onboarding completion down 4% and activation down 6%, so the intervention closest to the failing mechanism is onboarding simplification (memory_86, memory_31). I am verifying exactly those two because they may not be independent evidence: memory_31 (day 12, signup field reduction, SMB activation) and memory_86 (day 52, shortened onboarding, completion and time-to-value) could well be the same underlying experiment consolidated twice at different abstraction levels. If the archive shows one record behind both, my apparent two-source support collapses to one and I should size the test smaller; if they are genuinely distinct, a standard experiment is justified. Verification is spent on the direction I intend to act on, not on the ones I intend to reject.

I am explicitly declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing being the loudest signal this week. memory_73 is the one inherited record that reports a downstream cost: a 40% discount bought a 31% activation lift and 18% revenue gain but cost 12 points of renewal retention. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is a trade that borrows from renewals to flatter this quarter's activation number, and it would also anchor SMB price expectations in a way that is hard to unwind. The competitor's move creates urgency to match, which is precisely why it deserves suspicion rather than deference.

Secondary options: activation_messaging (memory_91) is a reasonable fallback and addresses the activation dip directly, but it treats the later symptom while onboarding completion — upstream of activation — is also falling; fixing the funnel entry is more likely to move both. referral_incentive (memory_57) was validated in established customers, not the price-sensitive SMB segment under pressure, so it is off-population. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is sound but addresses a segment that is not the one deteriorating.

Residual uncertainty I am not resolving away: all these memories are archived summaries whose effect sizes and durations I cannot fully audit, and none were measured under competitive price pressure, which may itself be the cause of the activation decline rather than any onboarding defect. If so, an onboarding fix will underperform its historical lift. Two further risks I am flagging rather than assuming away: cutting required signup fields can degrade lead qualification data and thus downstream sales routing quality, and prior lifts were measured on first-week activation, not on renewal — so I will instrument retention and lead-quality metrics, not just completion, before treating any win as real.
